text:
Morgan Frost has 13 points in 21 games for Calgary, six of them on the power play, and on a points-per-60 basis he is scoring well above his rate from last season. He broke a scoreless stretch with a goal in Saturday's 3-2 win in Los Angeles.

Look under the points and the shooting has nearly vanished. Over his last ten games he has generated 0.8 expected goals of his own (expected goals measure chance quality), against about 2.2 we'd expect from him, and he has put more than one shot on goal in only one of them. His assists are carrying the line. At five on five the Flames get 46.5% of the expected goals with him out there, roughly what they manage without him.

Some context helps. Evolving-Hockey had him playing with some of the weakest teammates in the league last season (bottom 7% by their impact) and still worth 1.7 wins. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 61% of his shots coming off the rush, and 61% of his entries as carries. Watch whether the shots come back; the assists won't keep coming on their own.
headline: Frost is producing without shooting
